_comment: Mutation testing for the API's credential path. Scoped deliberately to src/auth/ and its OWN unit tests: those are fully mocked, so they run clean inside Stryker's sandbox (which copies app/api only — tests that read the real filesystem or the tools/crawlers manifests outside it fail the dry run and abort the whole mutation run before any mutant is evaluated). Excluding tests one at a time would risk a false survivor whose killer was skipped; a tight scope avoids that. This is also the fairest possible test of the coverage figure: readTokens.js sits at 100% line AND 100% branch, so its score here says whether that number was earned. Enforced: see MUTATION FLOOR below. Run: cd app/api && npm run test:mutation:auth MUTATOR SET: StringLiteral and ObjectLiteral are disabled. permissions.js is largely a catalog of labels and descriptions; mutating that text produced 68 of its 72 survivors and dragged the score to 32.7% while saying nothing about behaviour — no sensible test asserts every description string. Disabling them makes the number mean 'did a wrong DECISION get caught', which is the question worth gating on. The cost is real and worth knowing: SQL strings stop being mutated too, so this cannot tell you a query is correct. That stays the contract tests' job (see app/api/CLAUDE.md — the unit mocks are SQL-blind by design). MUTATION FLOOR: `break` is set a few points under the measured score, and is a RATCHET — it only ever goes up. It is enforced by the weekly .github/workflows/js-mutation.yml (never on a PR: mutation is far heavier than the unit suite). The margin is not slack to spend, it absorbs the two things that legitimately move a score without anyone editing a test: a Stryker/vitest upgrade that changes which mutants are generated, and timeouts, which count as killed and can flip under CI load. Raise the floor when the score rises; never lower it to make a red run green — a drop means a test stopped discriminating. Measured 100.0% when the floor was set to 98. SCOPE GREW FOR #1166: src/auth/shareTokens.js and src/routes/matrix/shareRecipients.js joined it. Both are the same kind of code this config already measures — a token's shape and a caller's identity, decided by pure functions with their own fully-mocked unit tests — and together they are the WHOLE access decision for a shared matrix: shareTokens says which snapshot a URL resolves to, shareRecipients says who is allowed to open it. shareRecipients lives under src/routes/matrix/ rather than src/auth/ because it is the matrix share route's own rule, but it touches no database and no request object, so it runs clean in the sandbox exactly like the src/auth files; vitest.stryker.config.js names its test file explicitly rather than widening the include to src/routes/**, which would drag the filesystem-reading route tests back in. The route that USES them, src/routes/matrix/shares.js, is excluded with a reason below rather than mutated. SCOPE GREW FOR SEC-2026-09 M-06: src/routes/crawlers/crawlerGuards.js joined it. It is the whole decision for which crawler permissions an admin may grant (the worker-class admin permission is bootstrap-only) and which edits the built-in worker row refuses — pure functions plus one lookup through an injected pool, with a fully-mocked unit test (crawlerGuards.test.js) that touches no filesystem, so it runs clean in the sandbox like the files above. SCOPE GREW FOR SEC-2026-09 (M-08, I-04): src/secrets/masterKeyStore.js and src/config/fileSecrets.js joined it. They decide which secret the process runs with — where the vault master key is loaded from, when a legacy key file may be deleted, when a new key may be generated, and when a *_FILE secret replaces an environment variable. Their unit tests are self-contained (mocked database and vault, files only under os.tmpdir()), so they run clean in the sandbox; vitest.stryker.config.js names both test files. src/config/loadFileSecrets.js is excluded with a reason below.

mutationExclusions.src/lib/jobConfig.js: Reserved job-config keys stamped onto a queued crawler job (#1207). Recorded in THIS config because a written exclusion has to live in a Stryker config and the job-dispatch layer has none — every other module it sits between (src/routes/jobs/**, src/scheduler.js) is grandfathered in .ci/js-mutation-scope-baseline.json, and src/routes/jobs/urlPolicy.js below is already its nearest neighbour here. It is NOT part of this config's credential-path scope, so it is not in the mutate list: doing that would put a job-naming helper behind a floor that is meant to say something about the auth code. A dedicated stryker.jobs.config.json is the right home and cannot be added in isolation — tools/mutation/stryker_to_mutation_json.py derives the required report set from the configs, so a new config without a matching entry in the weekly workflow's hardcoded scope matrix would hard-fail the publish job (the same constraint already recorded for src/contexts/plugins/system-membership.helpers.js in stryker.matrix.config.json). Its decisions are each pinned by a case in src/lib/jobConfig.test.js, which drives the helper directly and is chosen to discriminate: a name that differs only by whitespace, a non-string name, and a null config.
mutationExclusions.src/routes/jobs/urlPolicy.js: Crawler connector-URL policy (SEC-2026-09 M-03). Cannot be mutated in this sandbox: which fields it checks comes from the real crawler manifests at ../../tools/crawlers (getUrlFields), and every test that exercises it — urlPolicy.test.js, jobs.routes.test.js, jobs.discover.test.js — resolves those manifests or the route stack outside app/api, so the dry run would abort (the same reason vitest.stryker.config.js keeps its include narrow). Its only decisions are two literal-true opt-in reads and a DNS-not-found pass-through; the address classification it relies on is lib/ssrfGuard.js.
mutationExclusions.src/lib/cappedBody.js: Byte-capped fetch body reader, moved verbatim out of llm/providers.js (which was itself outside every mutation scope) so the context-plugin feed fetch could share it — the move did not take anything out of measurement. Not added to this config's mutate list because two of its statements are equivalent mutants under the enabled mutators (the reader.cancel() rejection swallow in finally, and its empty arrow), which against this config's 98% floor would fail the weekly run on code whose behaviour is pinned: cappedBody.test.js asserts the exact-cap, one-over, declared-length and body-less cases.
mutationExclusions.src/routes/matrix/shares.js: Express route for /api/matrix/shares (#1166): its body is SQL text, HTTP status codes and the orchestration between them, and no route module in this repo is mutation-tested. The unit mocks it runs against are SQL-blind by design (app/api/CLAUDE.md), so a mutated query string would be killed only where a test happens to pin the text and would say nothing about whether the query returns the right rows — the question contract-tests/matrixShares.contract.test.js answers against a real PostgreSQL schema. The decisions worth pinning were deliberately moved OUT of this file and ARE mutated: token shape in auth/shareTokens.js, and who may open a share in ./shareRecipients.js.
mutationExclusions.src/config/loadFileSecrets.js: Two-statement side-effect entry point imported first by index.js and cli/auth-config.js: it calls applyFileSecrets() on process.env and logs the resolved variable names. Every decision lives in ./fileSecrets.js, which IS mutated. Its one test (config/fileSecrets.test.js) re-imports it against the real process.env and pins both the resolved value and the log line.
mutationExclusions.src/cli/rotate-master-key.js: Operator CLI (SEC-2026-09 L-05): argument/env parsing, one SQL transaction and console output around a single call to vault.rewrapDataKey(). The key-rewrapping decision itself lives in secrets/vault.js and is pinned end-to-end with real AES-GCM in cli/rotate-master-key.test.js and secrets/vault.test.js (a row re-wrapped by the wrong key fails to decrypt). What remains here is transaction orchestration against a SQL-blind pg mock, where a mutated statement is only killed if a test pins its text — the same reason route modules are not mutated.
mutationExclusions.src/routes/matrix/shareLinking.js: The share↔saved-matrix seam shared by shares.js's create and recipient-editing paths (#1202). Same kind of code as shares.js, excluded for the same reason: its weight is the recipient INSERT … ON CONFLICT statement, which the SQL-blind unit mocks cannot judge — contract-tests/matrixSharesSavedMatrix.contract.test.js runs it against a real PostgreSQL schema. What is left is a small status-carrying Error subclass and a one-line filter copy, both pinned directly by shareLinking.test.js (including the placeholder numbering across recipients).
